title: Inkling 2 Small Benchmarks, Pricing and API Costs
summary: What is Inkling 2 small is defined by its focus on efficient, logic-based reasoning tasks.
body_markdown:
## How to access inkling 2 small


Organizations can **bypass per-token SaaS fees** by hosting the model on private infrastructure, as Inkling 2 Small is available as an open-weights release on Hugging Face.


This availability means a DevOps team can pull the model repository directly into a private container registry. Sensitive proprietary data never leaves the corporate firewall during inference.


### Downloading Inkling 2 Small model weights


Hugging Face Hub serves as the primary distribution point for the model. The official repository provides the base weights and the instruct-tuned versions. By utilizing the Hugging Face CLI, developers can automate the synchronization of model assets into local storage volumes.


The time required to spin up new inference nodes in a Kubernetes cluster is reduced by this method. The repository includes the necessary configuration files for the Transformers library, so engineers can initialize the model with standard Python scripts rather than writing custom loaders.


### Inkling 2 Small hardware requirements


Running Inkling 2 Small at production scale requires a specific hardware footprint to maintain the low-latency response times expected of a specialized reasoning model.


The following table outlines the hardware commitments required based on the chosen quantization level, which dictates the total cost of ownership for the underlying compute.


Quantization Level VRAM Requirement Recommended Hardware Precision Impact


4-bit (NVFP4) 500 GB 2x B300 or 4x H200 Minimal for general logic


8-bit (MXFP8) 800 GB 4x B300 or 8x H200 Marginal gain over 4-bit, not considered practically meaningful


By selecting the 4-bit NVFP4 format, a business can run the model with as few as 2x NVIDIA B300 GPUs or 4x NVIDIA H200 GPUs, which requires less hardware than the 8-bit configuration.


However, the 8-bit MXFP8 deployment is necessary for high-precision logical tasks where rounding errors in weights could degrade the accuracy of complex mathematical outputs.


### Inkling 2 Small vision and multimodal support


Processing image inputs requires an additional vision encoder that operates alongside the primary reasoning MoE.


While the text-only 4-bit weights fit within 500GB of aggregated VRAM, activating the multimodal vision expert adds additional overhead to the primary memory pool, which means the system requires a significant hardware upgrade to maintain operational stability.


The model handles images by tokenizing visual features into a latent space that the reasoning chain can query as if it were text.


This allows the model to perform logical validation on visual data, such as checking if a physical signature is present on a scanned invoice.


To run these multimodal tasks at production speed, the software stack must include the FlashAttention-3 library and a CUDA 12.8+ environment. Without these specific drivers, the vision encoder will default to CPU offloading, which increases latency by a factor of ten.


### Third-party API providers supporting Inkling 2


Several specialized providers have added Inkling 2 Small to their inference catalogs for teams that prefer managed scaling over hardware maintenance.[Together](https://www.together.ai/models/inkling-2-small) AI and Groq provide serverless endpoints for the model, which eliminates the need for an upfront capital investment in GPU clusters.


These providers use high-throughput kernels to serve the model, so a developer can swap a single environment variable in their code to move from a local testing environment to a globally distributed API.
